findings.golden_ui_v3_clause: Accessible hierarchy and wayfinding: the current object/view title must participate in the page heading outline so screen-reader users can identify and navigate page sections without linearizing the full shell.
findings.human_centered_relationship: Name the current workspace semantically and preserve hierarchy for assistive navigation.
findings.user_consequence: Screen-reader users cannot use heading navigation to locate the current page or move through its top-level content; every view title is discoverable only as ordinary text in the reading order.
findings.reproducibility: Consistent in headless Chromium 151.0.7922.34 on all nine listed routes. Each has exactly one main landmark and zero h1/h2/h3/role=heading nodes inside main, while the visual page title is present.

affected_consumers.shared_authority: PageHeader is used by the standard Workbench shell and PatternPage renderers; other page consumers should be swept when repairing the shared primitive.

findings.baseline_comparison: Mapped surface identity and screenshots are unchanged from CHG-135 R16; the semantic heading defect was present in the comparison source where PageHeader uses the same label-only title pattern. No pixel regression asserted.
findings.smallest_bounded_fix: Render PageHeader title with a semantic level-one heading element/role while preserving the existing cui-page-title tokens and geometry; ensure a single page-level heading for shell and PatternPage compositions.
expected_closure_evidence: One meaningful h1/role=heading level 1 on each PageHeader consumer
No duplicate level-one heading for PatternPage inside a shell
Existing desktop/mobile screenshots retain the typography and dimensions
Keyboard/screen-reader heading outline reaches the current page identity
regression_risks: Default h1 margins/font styles can alter pixels if existing class/token styles do not reset them
Nested shell/pattern compositions may create duplicate heading levels
